newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senator proposes alternate stadium plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senator proposes alternate stadium plan.

text.p: California state Senator Quentin Kopp proposed that ticket buyers help finance a new stadium for the San Francisco 49ers football team, according to a published report on Wednesday.

Kopp, the leading opponent of the proposed stadium and mall complex, proposed a surcharge of $10 to $12 a ticket to generate $7.5 million to $10.8 million a year, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.
The money would pay principal and interest on a $100 million lease revenue bond issue that Kopp said he would support to help build the new stadium, the Chronicle said.
The team said Kopp's plan was "totally unacceptable and flawed in several ways."
San Franciscans will vote on the stadium project on June 3. The ballot measure calls for the sale of up to $100 million of bonds backed by stadium revenues.
